en.title: Hallelujah! What a Savior
en.author: Philip P. Bliss
stanzas:
[A]Man of Sorrows! [E7]what a [A]name
For the [D]Son of [A]God, who [E7]came
[A]Ruined [D]sinners to re[A]claim.
[D]Halle[A]lujah! [E7]What a [A]Savior!

Bearing shame and scoffing rude,
In my place condemned He stood;
Sealed my pardon with His blood.
Hallelujah! What a Savior!

When He comes, our glorious king,
All His ransomed home to bring,
Then anew His song we'll sing:
Hallelujah! What a Savior!

notes: First line and usual hymnal title are '"Man of Sorrows!" What a Name'; shipped under the worklist's title. Text is the Cyber Hymnal (hymnary.org/hymn/CYBER/2123). Hymnary lists the tune unnamed as '[Man of Sorrows, what a name]'; the Hymnology Archive records that it is most often called HALLELUJAH! WHAT A SAVIOR, also MAN OF SORROWS, and GETHSEMANE in England — the first is used here. Wording variants in other hymnals (hymnary's representative text, Psalter Hymnal Gray 1987): 'Guilty, helpless, lost were we; blameless Lamb of God was he', 'He was lifted up to die', and 'then anew this song we'll sing' where the Cyber Hymnal has 'His song'. Chords: printed key is B-flat Major, moved down a semitone to A per the guitar rule. Independently checked against Timeless Truths (URL appended; wording, 7.7.7.8 meter and B-flat key confirmed) — it capitalizes 'King' (st. 5) and quotes 'Full atonement!' and 'It is finished!'; the Cyber text's lowercase 'king' and unquoted lines are kept as printed.
